data.description:
## Problem

`gitutil.run_git_bounded` runs git through `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)`. When the bound expires, Python SIGKILLs only the direct `git` process. That causes two problems:

- The git process cannot run its signal cleanup. `git fetch` registers a handler that removes its `objects/pack/pack-*.keep` file on signal, and SIGKILL bypasses it.
- Children such as `index-pack` and `pack-objects` keep running after their parent dies. They are reparented to init, or to rebar-mcp when it is the container's PID 1.

A `.keep` file excludes its pack from every later repack. Until someone deletes it by hand, that pack is never consolidated.

## Evidence

- Production MCP tickets clone, inspected 2026-11-11. There were 12 `.keep` files, all reading `fetch-pack <pid> on <container-host>` and dated 2026-09-05 through 2026-09-15 UTC. No fetch was running. They were removed during the maintenance repair for bug `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek`.
- Local reproduction: a stand-in `git` that held a lock and had a child process was run through a `subprocess.run` timeout. The lock file stayed behind, and the child was reparented to PID 1. The same stand-in run under SIGTERM-first process-group reaping (`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`) cleaned up both.

## Scope boundary

Bug `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek` applied group reaping only to the explicit maintenance step. This ticket covers every other bounded git child: sync and push fetches and merges, and store commits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a bounded git child times out, its whole process group is reaped, SIGTERM first, so no git descendant outlives the call.
- [ ] A test proves that a bounded fetch interrupted by its bound leaves no `.keep` file and no surviving child process.
data.title: Bounded git timeout SIGKILLs only the parent, stranding fetch-pack .keep files and orphaning git children
